objects: unordered bag of instance feature vectors X = {x1,...,xK} in R^D
assumptions: MIL assumption: bag label positive iff at least one instance is positive
instances within a bag are independent and unordered (permutation invariance required)
guarantees: no formal theorem; empirical claim only
comparable or superior accuracy/AUC to prior MIL methods across benchmark, MNIST-bags, and histopathology datasets
formalism.operation: embed each instance with a neural net, compute a softmax-normalized attention weight per instance, aggregate via the attention-weighted sum, classify the aggregated bag representation

evidence_spans.objects: there is a bag of instances, X = {x1, . . . , xK}, that exhibit neither dependency nor ordering among each other.
evidence_spans.assumptions: These assumptions imply that a MIL model must be permutation-invariant.
evidence_spans.guarantees: We show empirically that our approach achieves comparable performance to the best MIL methods on benchmark MIL datasets and it outperforms other methods on a MNIST-based MIL dataset and two real-life histopathology datasets without sacrificing interpretability.
